amount.note: The Franchise Tax Board says every LLC doing business or organized in California pays this tax, even with no business activity, until the LLC is cancelled. A first-year exemption applied only to tax years that began before 2024, so a new LLC owes it in its first year.

annual.label: Statement of Information (Secretary of State)
annual.due: Due within 90 days of registering, then every two years.

notIncluded.reason: Only if you hire a registered agent. The agent sets the price, so it is not a state fee and is not in the total.

notIncluded.reason: Optional. Faster processing and certified copies cost extra and are not in the total.

notIncluded.label: Local business licenses and permits
notIncluded.reason: City, county and industry licenses depend on where the business operates and what it does. None are in the total.

content.intro: {state} charges an LLC two kinds of state cost: filing fees to the Secretary of State, and a yearly tax to the Franchise Tax Board that is due whether or not the LLC earns anything.

howItWorks.text: The Secretary of State charges a filing fee for the Articles of Organization. It also requires a Statement of Information soon after the LLC registers and again every two years, each with its own fee.

The Franchise Tax Board charges every LLC that is organized or doing business in {state} an annual tax, even if the LLC is not conducting business, until the LLC is cancelled. The first year's tax is due a few months after the LLC registers with the Secretary of State.
A first-year exemption from the annual tax covered only a limited run of earlier tax years. According to the Franchise Tax Board's page it has ended, so a new LLC owes the tax in its first year.
An LLC with larger {state} income also pays a fee that rises in steps with that income. It is not in the estimate because it depends on your own income.

faq.q: Do I owe the annual LLC tax in {state} if my LLC earns nothing?
faq.text: Yes. The Franchise Tax Board says the tax is due even if you are not conducting business, until you cancel your LLC.

faq.q: Is the Statement of Information a yearly filing?
faq.text: No. It is due within a set period after the LLC registers and every two years after that, so the estimate counts it on that schedule.

faq.q: Is there a way to avoid the first-year tax?
faq.text: The Franchise Tax Board describes a short-form cancellation for an LLC cancelled within its first year, which avoids the tax for that year. A first-year exemption that applied to earlier tax years has ended.
